title: Fuck Your AI Safeguards
lede: A senior product engineer vents after Claude Code halted a one-line security fix on their own product, arguing AI safeguards slow down defenders while attackers just use unrestricted models.

points: The block hit while the author was asking Claude Code for easy security improvements in a project they control.
Getting an exemption means waiting several business days, giving up data retention exemptions and handing over a government ID, with approval not guaranteed.
The author argues criminals simply turn to abliterated open-weight models, so the restrictions mainly stop legitimate users.
The issue was finally proven, fixed and verified with GLM 5.3 running on EU-hosted infrastructure.

points.text: Many commenters report fresh refusals on legitimate security work, from checking which Java versions were exposed to inspecting game binaries.
Several say they are shifting to open, self-hosted models because closed ones keep narrowing what they will help with.
Holders of access programs such as CVP and Daybreak say they still get blocked, including on fuzzers they could write months ago.
One commenter argues the episode shows Claude's constitution puts no real constraint on Anthropic itself once safeguards override it.
